newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland upholds large warnings on cigarette packs.
newsitem.headline: Poland upholds large warnings on cigarette packs.

text.p: Poland's parliament voted on Friday to go ahead with big new health warnings on cigarette packs.

Lower house deputies voted by 148 to 122 with 100 abstentions against a bid to scrap the warnings, which are much larger than the European norm and become compulsory at the end of the year under a 1995 law.
All cigarettes sold in Poland will have have to carry stark warnings over at least 30 percent of each large side of a pack.

Some deputies had argued that as European Union neighbours like Germany require only a much smaller message covering four percent, foreign products will have an advantage over local ones, especially when Poland joins the EU after the year 2000.
They said Poland should use the same size warnings as in the European Union.
Poles are among the world's heaviest smokers. About 90 billion cigarettes were sold last year.
